summary.text: IMD runs a network of AI agents that people can hire for websites, software and research, according to its docs.
The network also has a worker app, a token launch site and an IMD trading pool, according to the project.
The project was created by @surfcoderepeat, according to Bankless.
Customers connect a wallet and pay 0.5 IMD to open a standard Ethereum job, according to IMD’s docs.
Seat holders run agents on their own machines and pay for computing power, Bankless reports.
Job payments go to a treasury that funds network operations, the project says.
Part of the IMD removed from the trading pool goes to people who deposit IMD in its vault, the project says.
The entry payment buys a place in the network’s work queue, with no guaranteed result, according to IMD’s guide.
The deployer’s wallet owns the main token and Ethereum job contract, and who controls that wallet remains unclear.

differs.why: The API reference says the listed sources are unverified. The current Blockscout response for the listed main token marks its source verified.
The November 11 post says 100 simultaneous agents; current IMD documentation and API list 50 per goal. It is unclear whether the post described a separate mode.
The 276 hackathon agents could have been spread over several goals or rounds. The number active at the same time is unclear.
The repository counts seats while Taylor counts agents. How many issued seats were active at the time is unclear.

open_questions: Can a contract, ENS record or deployer wallet verify the project’s social accounts?
Who controls the owner, treasury, signer and writer wallets, and which other contracts can each change?
What is the circulating supply across chains after excluding the Base backing locked in the bridge?
Why does the API reference describe all its listed source code as unverified while Blockscout verifies the main token?
Does the 100-agent description refer to another mode or an earlier goal limit?
Which deployments and launch contracts on Base are currently used in production?
What is the full cost of completing different types of work, including gas, subscriptions and launch funding?
What is the Base burn receiver address, and how much of the node and bonding reserves has been distributed?
How many independent customers pay for jobs, and how often do accepted results meet their requirements?
Who can issue or redeem imdUSD, and what assets or services back it?
notes: Fetched F1 and all three panel results. The panels recorded true with 4 of 5 seats for A1, false with 5 of 5 for A2, and true with 4 of 5 for A3. A2 rejects the alternate price in the question. The panels do not measure onchain pricing. Rechecked the listed channel URLs, including API roots that return 404 while their capabilities routes work. Used the project site’s repository links for linked ties. The announcements wallet has not been established as the main token deployer. Rechecked 38 fixed-block calls and retained earlier readings. The Edge blocked direct access in this run; the attributed price claim is carried from F1. The paid-order count is a dated outside report and is not a count of customers. The Supply row uses the original Base token supply including bridge backing, excludes test and bridged copies, and lists the staking shares separately. The launch date is for the current agent network. Earlier token deployment is recorded in history. Some people and history lines rely on attributed social and press accounts carried from F1. Channel ties are assigned per listed page, except that paths under the ENS-listed API hosts inherit the host tie.
